questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect form of the question:
The petitioner said to the clerk, "Are the certified court records ready for inspection?"

options.text: The petitioner asked the clerk if the certified court records were ready for inspection.
The petitioner asked the clerk if were the certified court records ready for inspection.
The petitioner asked that whether the certified court records were ready for inspection.
The petitioner enquired the clerk if the certified court records were ready for inspection.

questions.explanation: Yes/No question auxiliary 'Are' se shuru ho raha hai. Connective 'if' lagega. Plural subject 'the certified court records' auxiliary 'were' se pehle aayega. Option (A) bilkul accurate hai. Option (B) mein inverted auxiliary 'were' subject se pehle chhod di gayi hai. Option (C) mein fatal 'that whether' double conjunction blunder hai. Option (D) mein 'enquired' listener object ke sath 'of' ke bina use kiya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Yes/No question conversion with declarative word order.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.subtopic: Yes/No Question with 'Do' Auxiliary & Adverbial Shift
questions.question:
Convert the interrogative sentence into Indirect Speech:
The system administrator said to me, "Do you encounter this network latency every day?"

options.text: The system administrator asked me if I did encounter that network latency every day.
The system administrator asked me whether I encountered that network latency every day.
The system administrator asked me that whether I encountered this network latency every day.
The system administrator enquired me if I encountered that network latency every day.

questions.explanation: Auxiliary 'do' affirmative reported statement mein drop ho jati hai aur verb 'encounter' Simple Past 'encountered' ban jati hai. Demonstrative 'this' ➔ 'that' banta hai. Connective 'whether' ke baad subject 'I' pehle aata hai. Option (B) 100% correct hai. Option (A) emphatic auxiliary 'did encounter' use karta hai. Option (C) mein 'that whether' double connective hai aur 'this' unshifted hai. Option (D) mein 'enquired' ke baad 'of' missing hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01 & RC-04: 'Do' auxiliary removal, Simple Past conversion, and demonstrative shift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.subtopic: Yes/No Question with 'Did' Auxiliary (Simple Past ➔ Past Perfect)
questions.question:
Select the correct Indirect Speech version:
The judge said to the witness, "Did you observe any suspicious movement near the registry building last night?"

options.text: The judge asked the witness whether he had observed any suspicious movement near the registry building the previous night.
The judge asked the witness whether he observed any suspicious movement near the registry building last night.
The judge asked the witness if had he observed any suspicious movement near the registry building the previous night.
The judge told the witness whether he had observed any suspicious movement near the registry building the previous night.

questions.explanation: Simple Past question ('Did you observe') backshift hokar Past Perfect ('had observed') banega. 'Last night' badal kar 'the previous night' banega. Connective 'whether' ke baad subject 'he' auxiliary se pehle aayega. Option (A) bilkul flawless hai. Option (B) mein tense aur time expression dono unshifted hain. Option (C) mein 'had he' inverted order retain hai. Option (D) mein question ke liye reporting verb 'told' use kiya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Past tense backshift with whether and time shift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Identify the grammatically correct Indirect transformation:
The advocate said to the client, "Do you intend to file an appeal or not?"

options.text: The advocate asked the client if or not he intended to file an appeal.
The advocate asked the client whether or not he intended to file an appeal.
The advocate asked the client that whether he intended to file an appeal or not.
The advocate enquired the client whether or not he intended to file an appeal.

questions.explanation: Jab question mein immediate 'or not' jud raha ho, toh standard exam grammar mein connective strictly 'whether' hota hai ('whether or not'). 'If or not' non-standard hai. Main verb 'intend' Simple Past 'intended' ban gayi. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) non-standard 'if or not' use karta hai. Option (C) 'that whether' double conjunction blunder contain karta hai. Option (D) mein 'enquired' ke baad 'of' missing hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Mandatory 'whether or not' in explicit alternative conditions.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Convert into Indirect Speech:
The judicial assistant said to the applicant, "Where did you procure this stamp paper?"

options.text: The judicial assistant asked the applicant where did he procure that stamp paper.
The judicial assistant asked the applicant where he had procured that stamp paper.
The judicial assistant asked the applicant that where he had procured that stamp paper.
The judicial assistant enquired the applicant where he had procured this stamp paper.

questions.explanation: Wh-word 'where' connective retain hoga. Simple Past question ('did procure') Past Perfect ('had procured') banega aur subject 'he' auxiliary se pehle aayega. Demonstrative 'this' ➔ 'that' convert hoga. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein question structure 'did he procure' retain hai. Option (C) mein 'that where' double conjunction blunder hai. Option (D) mein 'enquired' ke baad 'of' missing hai aur 'this' unshifted hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Wh-question inversion removal and Simple Past to Past Perfect backshift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.subtopic: Wh-Question (Why) with Continuous Aspect & Pronoun Shifts
questions.question:
Select the correct Indirect conversion:
The bench secretary said to the computer operator, "Why are you altering the official database entries?"

options.text: The bench secretary asked the computer operator why was he altering the official database entries.
The bench secretary asked the computer operator that why he was altering the official database entries.
The bench secretary asked the computer operator why he was altering the official database entries.
The bench secretary asked the computer operator why he is altering the official database entries.

questions.explanation: Wh-word 'why' connective banega. Present Continuous auxiliary 'are' backshift hokar singular 'was' banegi aur subject 'he' ke BAAD shift hogi ('why he was altering'). Option (C) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein inversion 'was he' retain hai. Option (B) mein 'that why' double conjunction hai. Option (D) mein tense ko backshift nahi kiya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Wh-word with statement word order in continuous aspect.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly applies the reporting verb preposition rule?

options.text: The inspector enquired the watchman what time the judge had departed.
The inspector enquired of the watchman what time the judge had departed.
The inspector enquired of the watchman what time had the judge departed.
The inspector asked to the watchman what time the judge had departed.

questions.explanation: Verb 'enquired' listener object ke sath mandatory preposition 'of' leti hai ('enquired of the watchman'). Uske baad connective 'what time' ke sath assertive word order 'the judge had departed' aaya hai. Option (B) 100% correct hai. Option (A) mein 'of' missing hai. Option (C) mein inversion 'had the judge departed' retain hai. Option (D) mein 'asked' ke baad inappropriate preposition 'to' lagaya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: 'Enquired of + Object' vs 'Asked + Object'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Convert the command into Indirect Speech:
The registrar said to the assistant, "Verify the digital signature immediately."

options.text: The registrar ordered the assistant to verify the digital signature immediately.
The registrar ordered to the assistant to verify the digital signature immediately.
The registrar ordered the assistant that he should verify the digital signature immediately.
The registrar requested the assistant to verify the digital signature immediately.

questions.explanation: Authoritative command ke liye reporting verb 'ordered' aayegi. Base verb 'Verify' non-finite infinitive 'to verify' mein convert hogi. Option (A) bilkul flawless hai. Option (B) mein 'ordered to the assistant' non-standard prepositional usage hai. Option (C) imperative ki jagah redundant 'that he should' clause use karta hai. Option (D) administrative hierarchy ke contrary 'requested' use karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Imperative commands require 'ordered + object + to + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Convert the request into Indirect Speech:
The applicant said to the clerk, "Please stamp my application receipt."

options.text: The applicant requested the clerk to please stamp his application receipt.
The applicant requested the clerk to stamp his application receipt.
The applicant told the clerk to stamp my application receipt.
The applicant ordered the clerk to stamp his application receipt.

questions.explanation: 'Please' aane par reporting verb 'requested' lagti hai aur polite marker 'please' drop ho jata hai. Verb 'stamp' banegi 'to stamp' aur 1st person possessive 'my' applicant ke anusaar 'his' banega. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein 'please' ko retain karke redundancy create ki gayi hai. Option (C) mein pronoun 'my' unshifted hai aur polite sense lost hai. Option (D) subordinate to clerk context mein authoritarian 'ordered' use karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Elimination of 'please' in reported requests.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech version:
The judge said to the witness, "Do not disclose the identity of the informant."

options.text: The judge ordered the witness to not disclose the identity of the informant.
The judge ordered the witness not to disclose the identity of the informant.
The judge ordered the witness that he should not disclose the identity of the informant.
The judge forbade the witness not to disclose the identity of the informant.

questions.explanation: Negative command 'Do not + V1' ko report karne ka standard format 'not to + V1' ('not to disclose') hota hai. 'Not' particle 'to' se pehle aayega. Option (B) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) split infinitive 'to not disclose' use karta hai jo formal exams mein secondary hota hai. Option (C) unnecessary lengthy clause hai. Option (D) fatal double negative 'forbade... not to' contain karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Standard negative imperative placement 'not to + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly expresses prohibition using the verb 'forbade'?

options.text: The invigilator forbade the candidates not to communicate during the examination.
The invigilator forbade to the candidates to communicate during the examination.
The invigilator forbade the candidates to communicate during the examination.
The invigilator forbade the candidates from communicating not during the examination.

questions.explanation: 'Forbade' inherently negative verb hai, isliye iske baad aane wala infinitive strictly POSITIVE ('to communicate') hona chahiye bina kisi 'not' ke. Direct object 'the candidates' bina preposition ke aayega. Option (C) 100% correct hai. Option (A) fatal double negative 'forbade... not to' blunder hai. Option (B) mein 'forbade to the candidates' non-standard preposition hai. Option (D) ungrammatical syntax hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: 'Forbade + object + to + V1' takes zero extra negative particles.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Convert the proposal into Indirect Speech:
The senior assistant said to his colleagues, "Let's digitize the old case files today."

options.text: The senior assistant suggested to his colleagues that they should digitize the old case files that day.
The senior assistant suggested his colleagues that they should digitize the old case files today.
The senior assistant ordered his colleagues to digitize the old case files that day.
The senior assistant proposed his colleagues to digitize the old case files that day.

questions.explanation: 'Let's' mutual suggestion indicate karta hai. Reporting verb 'suggested' listener object ke sath preposition 'to' leti hai ('suggested to his colleagues'). Conjunction 'that' ke baad modal 'should' ke sath 'they should digitize' banta hai, aur 'today' ➔ 'that day' convert hota hai. Option (A) bilkul flawless hai. Option (B) mein 'suggested' ke baad 'to' missing hai aur 'today' unshifted hai. Option (C) proposal ko command bana deta hai. Option (D) incorrect infinitive syntax use karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: 'Let's' proposals require 'suggested to + object + that they should + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Convert the exclamatory sentence into Indirect Speech:
The advocate said, "Alas! The principal witness has turned hostile!"

options.text: The advocate exclaimed with sorrow that the principal witness had turned hostile.
The advocate exclaimed with joy that the principal witness had turned hostile.
The advocate said with sorrow that the principal witness has turned hostile.
The advocate exclaimed with regret that had the principal witness turned hostile.

questions.explanation: Interjection 'Alas!' sorrow aur grief express karta hai, isliye reporting phrase 'exclaimed with sorrow' banega aur 'Alas!' drop ho jayega. Conjunction 'that' aayega. Present Perfect 'has turned' backshift hokar Past Perfect 'had turned' banega. Option (A) bilkul perfect hai. Option (B) contextually opposite emotion 'joy' use karta hai. Option (C) mein tense backshift omit kiya gaya hai ('has turned'). Option (D) assertive statement ki jagah inverted word order use karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Exclamatory sorrow with 'Alas!' shifts to 'exclaimed with sorrow that...'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.subtopic: Exclamatory 'How' Adjective Transformation to Assertive with 'Very'
questions.question:
Select the correct Indirect form of the exclamation:
The spectator said, "How gracefully the senior advocate presented the constitutional argument!"

options.text: The spectator exclaimed that how gracefully the senior advocate had presented the constitutional argument.
The spectator exclaimed with admiration that the senior advocate had presented the constitutional argument very gracefully.
The spectator exclaimed with wonder that did the senior advocate present the constitutional argument gracefully.
The spectator told that the senior advocate presented the constitutional argument very gracefully.

questions.explanation: 'How gracefully...!' admiration express karta hai. Indirect speech mein sentence assertive statement banta hai: 'How' drop hokar intensity convey karne ke liye manner adverb se pehle 'very' judta hai ('very gracefully'). Simple Past 'presented' backshift hokar Past Perfect 'had presented' banta hai. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) exclamatory syntax 'how gracefully' retain karta hai. Option (C) statement ko interrogative inversion bana deta hai. Option (D) reporting verb 'told' bina listener object ke use karta hai aur tense backshift omit karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: 'How + Adverb/Adjective' exclamations shift to assertive statements with 'very'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.subtopic: Optative Sentence with 'May God...' Prayer Formula
questions.question:
Convert the optative prayer into Indirect Speech:
The saint said to the king, "May God bless your kingdom with enduring peace!"

options.text: The saint prayed that God might bless his kingdom with enduring peace.
The saint prayed that might God bless his kingdom with enduring peace.
The saint wished that God may bless your kingdom with enduring peace.
The saint prayed to the king that God might bless his kingdom with enduring peace.

questions.explanation: Almighty God se prarthna ke liye reporting verb 'prayed' lagti hai. Conjunction 'that' ke baad divine subject 'God' pehle aayega aur modal 'May' backshift hokar 'might' banega jo subject ke BAAD aayega ('that God might bless'). 2nd person possessive 'your' king ke anusaar 'his' banega. Option (A) bilkul flawless hai. Option (B) inverted order 'might God' retain karta hai. Option (C) unshifted 'may' aur unshifted pronoun 'your' contain karta hai. Option (D) 'prayed to the king' likhta hai jiska meaning nikalta hai ki saint ne king se prarthna ki (jabki prarthna God se ki gayi thi).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Optative prayer syntax with 'that + Subject + might + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07
